title: C01: frame routes query nonexistent stage_states.state_data by project_id; visual capsule id always undefined for frame image jobs
summary: Five frame routes select state_data from stage_states filtered by project_id and stage_number 3. stage_states has no project_id and no state_data column in any migration, and the Supabase error is discarded by destructuring only data, so visualStyleCapsuleId is undefined. Frame image jobs are then created with visualStyleCapsuleId undefined, so ImageGenerationService skips capsule context for them.

flags.tested: N (no test references state_data or the frames capsule lookup)

Wave-1 PROV-0009 says frame jobs 'never receive a style capsule id'; precisely, the five routes above pass undefined, and no other frame image-job creator exists (only zero-cost copy rows at frames.ts:1930, 2076 and frameGenerationService.ts:1095 insert status completed with no generation). title: C02: projects.writing_style_capsule_id and projects.visual_style_capsule_id have no writer; only the migration adds them and 4 read sites consume them
summary: Across backend/src (non-test), backend/migrations, backend/scripts, backend/quickies-sql and src, no statement writes these two columns. The only DDL is migration 004 ADD COLUMN. Project create (POST insert), PATCH whitelist, and the SQL UPDATE projects in migrations 042-044 never include them, so the columns are NULL for every project. The read sites therefore always see null and fall through or skip capsule loading.
evidence: backend/src/routes/projects.ts:3584 and 3740-3743 (read in Stage 9 prompt generation)
src/types/project.ts:91 (ProjectParams has writingStyleCapsuleId only; no visualStyleCapsuleId)
notes: Wave-1 V2/V9 claim is correct. Count check: 5 conditional read sites (contextManager.ts:498 and :499 in one block; frames.ts:569 and :2216; projects.ts:3740) plus 3 select lists (frames.ts:527, :2156; projects.ts:3584). Wave-1 V2 WD-IMPL-FACT-0019 'read in five backend places' is consistent with this count. Writing capsule has a separate real source: Stage 1/2/3 send writing_style_capsule_id in request bodies (src/lib/services/treatmentService.ts:68, beatService.ts:65, scriptService.ts:89) and llm.ts:236-245 reads it as a prompt variable; none persist it to projects. The visual capsule's real persisted source is stage_states content locked_visual_style_capsule_id (src/components/pipeline/Stage5Assets.tsx:227), not projects. contextManager.ts:499 falls back to stage1 projectParams.visualStyleCapsuleId, which no src code sets (grep visualStyleCapsuleId in src/components/pipeline/Stage1InputMode.tsx and src/types/project.ts returns nothing for it), so that fallback is also always undefined.

title: C03: Phase A unlock warning dialog never opens; the client falls through and auto-confirms the unlock, so the cascade runs with no warning
summary: Backend returns the 409 impact body with downstreamStages and message nested under details. ProjectView.handlePhaseAUnlock reads result.downstreamStages at top level, which is undefined, so it takes the else branch: it sets the stage, sets impact to null, and calls handleConfirmPhaseAUnlock, which POSTs confirm=true. The draft version is inserted and downstream locked stages get outdated rows with no dialog shown.

summary: scenes.stage_locks is added only by backend/quickies-sql/add_stage_locks.sql, not by any migration, and six route handlers select it (projects.ts shots/lock :2845 and shots/unlock :3020; sceneStageLocks.ts GET :18, lock :56, unlock :145, relock :290), so a DB built from migrations alone makes shot-list lock return 404 SCENE_NOT_FOUND and GET stage-locks return 404. Precision additions: (1) the route 'ambiguous' state needs a shot with no location_asset_id and no manual source, and the resolver to report a top-second gap of at most 0.06 with top at least 0.56; (2) the 0.72 cut in the route is the same constant used for auto-apply (shouldApplyResolution, locationResolverService.ts:441-445), so the route 'resolved' threshold equals the auto-apply threshold, while composition's 0.8 has no named constant; (3) composition returns candidates always empty (continuityCompositionService.ts:247), so the composition output carries no candidate list. title: C08: migration runner sends each ';'-split fragment to an 'exec' RPC that no repo file defines; migration 005 Step 4 uses invalid ADD CONSTRAINT ... WHERE syntax; duplicate 022 and 024 pairs sort deterministically
summary: scripts/run-migrations.ts calls DatabaseService.runMigration for every .sql file in sorted order. runMigration splits the file on ';' and calls supabase.rpc('exec', {query}); on any error it throws, so the runner stops at the first statement when no exec function exists. No CREATE FUNCTION exec exists in backend, src or migrations. Migration 005 line 22-25 uses ADD CONSTRAINT ... UNIQUE (user_id, name) WHERE library_id IS NULL, which PostgreSQL's ALTER TABLE grammar does not accept. Both 022 and 024 pairs are independent of each other and sort by file name.

flags.functional: N as written (exec RPC absent in repo; 21 of 46 migrations contain $$ bodies that ';' splitting breaks)
flags.tested: N (no test file references runMigration or run-migrations)

notes: Verdict CONFIRMED for the runner and exec RPC claim (wave-1 C WD-IMPL-FACT-0150 is accurate). Migration 005 syntax claim: static check against the PostgreSQL ALTER TABLE grammar, which allows index_parameters (INCLUDE, WITH, USING INDEX TABLESPACE) and deferrability on UNIQUE table constraints but no WHERE predicate; a partial unique requires CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... WHERE. Not executed (no database access allowed); the parser was not available offline. Whether live DB has style_capsules_user_name_unique is UNKNOWN. The duplicate-number pairs are not order-dependent: the 022 pair and the 024 pair have no cross-references (022_scene_asset_generation_attempts creates tables and ALTERs scene_asset_instances, 024_scene_asset_suggestions creates scene_asset_suggestions referencing scenes and project_assets, neither depends on the sibling file). The runner sort is JavaScript default string sort, so ordering is deterministic. The message text in database.ts:54 says the migration must be run in the Supabase SQL Editor, which is the operational path the code itself names.
